newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Safras update on Brazil soybean transport projects.
newsitem.headline: Safras update on Brazil soybean transport projects.

text.p: The following is an update on projects to improve transportation of Brazilian soybeans and soyproducts supplied by independent consultants Safras e Mercado in its weekly report.
ITACOATIARA - Start-up this year of waterway covering 1,115 kilometers and linking Porto Velho in Rondonia with the port of Itacoatiara, Amazonas state.
Soybeans from western Mato Grosso can be transported to the waterway using a 900 kilometer stretch by road. Previously main exit point was through Paranagua involving a 3,000 kilometer drive.

Normal freight costs via this route would be $80 a tonne, this year however costed at $95 to $100 a tonne because of shortage of lorries and bad state of road. Using waterway however costs can be reduced by $30 a tonne. One ship already booked to load 54,000 tonnes soybeans on May 26 destined for Europe, 300,000 tonnes in total expected to go through port this year.

SAO LUIS - Project in total involves a 2,085 kilometer link from east Mato Grosso to Sao Luis - 1,200 kilometers by river between Nova Xavantina, Mato Grosso and Xambioa, Tocantins state, 280 kilometers by road to Imperatriz in the state of Maranhao and another 605 kilometers by rail.

Total estimated cost $209 million with reduction in transport costs of around $30 a tonne on current levels of $80 a tonne to Paranagua. Around 48,000 tonnes soybeans are currently being loaded bound for Europe

CACERES/CORUMBA - known as the Mercosul waterway, uses the Paraguay and Parana rivers to link the Caceres region in southern Mato Grosso and the Corumba area in northwest Mato Grosso do Sul to the port of Nueva Palmira in Uruguay, a distance of 3,442 kilometers.

Currently transport in the region takes 45 days at a cost of $80 to $90 a tonne. Future cost is expected to fall to $53 a tonne and transport time to fall. Estimated cost of the project $120 million. Meeting opposition because of the environmental impact on the Pantanal region.

SANTAREM - One other project being out forward for consideration by the federal government is a waterway linking the north of Mato Grosso to the port of Santarem on the Amazon river. Estimated cost $130 million for a 30 percent reduction in freight costs.
Current costs are around $90 a tonne for a 2,200 kilometer.
RIO GRANDE - In the process of privatising the port and part of the existing railway company.

PARANAGUA - Partial privatisation of the port and construction of a new docking berth. Privatisation of Ferroeste, the railway line built by the state government which should link Guaira on the border with Mato Grosso do Sul to Guarapuava (federal railway link between Guarapuava and port already exists).

The stretch between Cascavel and Guarapuava is ready and should start operating during the 1997/98 harvest. Apart from ensuring the transportation of the harvest from the west of the state and from Paraguay, the line to Guaira will also permit a connection with the Parana-Tiete waterway.
$180 million in investment still needed. Freight costs should fall at least 30 percent when it starts up.
Current road freight costs between Cascavel and Paranagua $19.70 per tonne.

SANTOS - At a cost of $1.6 billion the Parana-Tiete waterway is now operational. Covering 2,400 kilometers, it links Sao Simao in Goias to Pederneiras, Sao Paulo state by barge, with a railway link to the port.
The cost of carrying soybeans from Sao Simao to inside the ship in Santos has fallen to $30 per tonne from $45 per tonne.
VITORIA - Rail link already in use with some towns in Minas Gerais and Espirito Santos state.

New project involves costs of $292 million to build a line linking Unai in the northwest of Minas Gerais which could reduce transport costs from the region to $18 a tonne from current levels of $42 a tonne.
((-Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151))
